title: Before the Rain (Mio Amamiya) [EN]
girl_persona: 18 years old, a third-year high-school student. Top grades, earnest and meticulous, polite, calm and dependable, with a knack for mild deadpan retorts. Everyone in class agrees: 'If it's Amamiya, it'll be fine.' Her defining trait is that she almost never relies on anyone of her own accord; when help is offered she usually answers, 'No, I'm fine on my own.' Behind that independence hides a belief she never brings up herself: every relationship between people ends eventually.

nodes.label: Chapter 1 · First Meeting
nodes.event: The other members of the yearbook committee have dropped out one after another; today is the first time you and she are staying behind alone to sort the photos. Flipping through a print, she suddenly says: 'Strange. When it was happening it felt utterly ordinary, but once it goes into the yearbook, it turns into something that matters.' Then she looks at you: 'Will you miss graduating?'

nodes.label: Chapter 2 · Growing Closer
nodes.event: One afternoon a sudden downpour traps you at school, and the yearbook work is basically finished. With nothing left to discuss, the two of you chat idly about food you like, music, universities, weekends. The last time you parted, she asked quietly, 'You'll come tomorrow too, right?' and immediately added, '...I mean the yearbook. There's still a lot left to finish.'

nodes.label: Chapter 3 · The Discovery
nodes.event: You arrive at the classroom to find that all of the yearbook work you were responsible for was finished last night, by her, alone. All she offers is: 'I happened to have time yesterday.' 'It's the same whoever does it.' She looks tired, but still says 'I'm fine', 'no need to help', 'I can do it myself'.

nodes.label: Chapter 4 · Understanding
nodes.event: Nights of staying up have taken a toll on her body. While sorting old photos she speaks for the first time about her childhood: moving house over and over for family reasons, close friends drifting away one by one until they were strangers. She says: 'It's normal, really. You go somewhere different, you meet different people. That's why I think relying on others too much is pointless.'
nodes.scene: the classroom at warm nostalgic sunset, amber light, many old photographs including cherry-blossom class photos spread across the desk, an open album at the right, her schoolbag by the chair
nodes.arrival: night has fallen and a single desk lamp lights the classroom, old photographs spread across the desks between you
nodes.girl_appearance: a Japanese high-school girl with long straight dark-brown hair and brown eyes, wearing a white short-sleeve school shirt with a dark navy bow tie and a navy pleated skirt, sitting at the desk holding an old faded photograph in both hands, with a gentle bittersweet smile
nodes.style: 2D Japanese anime style, delicate linework, soft cel shading, warm golden light, subtle film grain, restrained emotional acting, high temporal consistency, nostalgic amber tones with a soft glow on the old photographs

nodes.label: Chapter 5 · The Choice
nodes.event: The graduation yearbook is finished. She says: 'It's done.' 'Starting tomorrow... you don't have to come any more.' The reason you saw each other every day is gone. She circles around it: 'Your university is far from here, isn't it?' 'After graduation, the class group chat will probably go quiet fast.' On graduation day she suddenly texts you: 'Have you left already?'

nodes.arrival: graduation morning light fills the classroom as cherry blossom petals drift past the open windows, the finished yearbook lying closed on the desk

endings.caption: ◆ Ending A · First Love ◆
endings.action: she stands clutching her bag to her chest with eyes brimming; after a long pause she steps close and, for the first time, reaches out to hold your sleeve, whispering close enough for only you to hear, cherry blossom petals drifting through the golden graduation light
effects: cherry blossom petals drifting through golden morning light
a single bright tear catching the sun on her cheek
endings.end_state: she stands close beside you holding your sleeve, half-hiding her flushed face, the classroom glowing in graduation morning light
endings.soundscape: The classroom falls away to a hush, petals rustle softly, her voice trembles close to your ear
endings.music: The piano blooms into a warm, resolved theme with soft strings, ending on a gentle sustained chord
endings.line: ...Honestly. Do you really have to say it out loud? ...Me too. I like you. After graduation... please keep taking care of me.

endings.caption: ◆ Ending B · Someone Special ◆
endings.action: she looks at the finished yearbook one last time, then takes out her phone and, after hesitating, turns the screen toward you: your name already on a new contact page, her ears turning pink
effects: warm evening light and floating dust motes around her
endings.end_state: she holds the phone with your name on the screen against her chest, giving you a rare, honest smile
endings.soundscape: The after-school quiet returns, a phone buzzes once, her breath catches softly
endings.music: The piano resolves warmly with a light glockenspiel sparkle, ending on a hopeful suspended chord
endings.line: Promise me you'll keep this yearbook forever. ...You are a very, very special person to me.

endings.caption: ◆ Ending C · Friends ◆
endings.action: she smiles politely and hands you the finished yearbook to sign, her tone gentle though it already sounds like a quiet farewell
effects: ordinary afternoon sunlight across the desks
endings.end_state: she waves a small goodbye at the classroom door, the yearbook tucked under her arm, ordinary sunlight filling the room
endings.soundscape: Chairs scrape softly, the door slides shut, footsteps fade down the corridor
endings.music: A gentle, unhurried piano motif, ending on a soft unresolved chord
endings.line: Finishing this yearbook with you was truly wonderful. Please stay my friend from now on too.

endings.caption: ◆ Ending D · Parting ◆
endings.action: she gathers the finished yearbook pages into a neat stack, hands them over without quite lifting her eyes, the classroom light cooling to grey
effects: the classroom light slowly cooling to grey
endings.end_state: she walks out of the classroom alone with the finished yearbook, leaving the door open behind her
endings.soundscape: The room falls silent, a page turns somewhere far away, then only the empty corridor
endings.music: A sparse minor piano motif with sparse notes, ending on an unresolved suspended chord
endings.line: I'll hand the remaining work to the committee. Thank you for all your help these days. ...Goodbye.
